components.note: 乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'
囗 (an enclosure) — a garden like 园 is an enclosed area of land.
元 (yuán) is close in sound to 园 — an exact match.

example.hanzi: 迪士尼乐园是很多孩子的梦想目的地。
example.pinyin: Díshìní lèyuán shì hěnduō háizi de mèngxiǎng mùdìdì.
example.english: Disneyland is the dream destination for many children.
example.fact: Disneyland in Anaheim, California, opened in 1955 and was designed under Walt Disney's close personal supervision, from groundbreaking to opening day. It remains the only Disney theme park Walt himself oversaw in full, and its early construction budget was famously so tight that he borrowed against his own life insurance policy to help fund it.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

example.hanzi: 土壤中缺乏加里会影响植物生长。
example.pinyin: Tǔrǎng zhōng quēfá jiālǐ huì yǐngxiǎng zhíwù shēngzhǎng.
example.english: A lack of potassium in the soil affects plant growth.
example.fact: Potassium is the seventh most abundant element in Earth's crust and is essential for plant growth and human nerve and muscle function. Bananas are often cited as a top potassium source, though foods like potatoes, white beans, and spinach actually contain more potassium per serving.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms and legs spread) depicts a human figure.
口 here stands for an opening or dwelling; a person stepping away from it gave 去 its meaning 'to leave, to go away.'
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

example.hanzi: 编辑建议我去掉这段多余的描述。
example.pinyin: Biānjí jiànyì wǒ qùdiào zhè duàn duōyú de miáoshù.
example.english: The editor suggested I remove this redundant passage.
example.fact: CRISPR-Cas9 works like a pair of molecular scissors that can precisely cut out, or remove, a targeted sequence of DNA. The technique, developed by Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier, earned them the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

components.note: The 田-shaped top pictures a large, strange head.
儿-shaped legs below trace a crouching, spindly body, together giving 鬼 the shape of a ghostly figure.
氵 (water) — 混 originally described muddy, mixed water.
昆 (kūn) gives a sound distantly related to hùn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他整天在外面鬼混,不好好学习。
example.pinyin: Tā zhěngtiān zài wàimiàn guǐhùn, bù hǎohǎo xuéxí.
example.english: He fools around outside all day instead of studying properly.
example.fact: The three-toed sloth spends up to 15 to 20 hours a day resting in trees and moves so slowly that algae grows directly on its fur, giving it a greenish camouflage. It is one of the most extreme low-energy lifestyles documented among mammals.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) is close in sound to 情 — a close match differing only in tone.
心 (heart) — 愿 relates to a heartfelt wish or desire
原 (yuán) has a loose sound connection to 愿's reading yuàn

example.hanzi: 她情愿一个人旅行,也不愿意跟团。
example.pinyin: Tā qíngyuàn yí gè rén lǚxíng, yě bú yuànyì gēn tuán.
example.english: She would rather travel alone than join a tour group.
example.fact: In 1978, Japanese explorer Naomi Uemura became the first person to reach the North Pole alone, traveling by dog sled from Ellesmere Island. A decade earlier, he had also completed a solo raft descent of the Amazon River, part of a career built around solitary expeditions.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 担 relates to carrying something, often on a shoulder pole
旦 (dàn) is close in sound to 担's reading dān, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) is a faint match in sound to 保's reading bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 银行要求有人担保才能批准贷款。
example.pinyin: Yínháng yāoqiú yǒurén dānbǎo cái néng pīzhǔn dàikuǎn.
example.english: The bank requires someone to guarantee the loan before it can be approved.
example.fact: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, founded in Siena, Italy, in 1472, is the world's oldest continuously operating bank. It originally issued loans against pawned goods as collateral, an early form of a guaranteed loan.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) is a faint match in sound to 场's reading chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) is a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 这块场地将用于建设新体育馆。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài chǎngdì jiāng yòng yú jiànshè xīn tǐyùguǎn.
example.english: This site will be used to build a new stadium.
example.fact: The Panathenaic Stadium in Athens, rebuilt for the first modern Olympics in 1896, sits on the same site as an ancient Greek stadium from the 4th century BC. It is made almost entirely of white marble.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 液 names any liquid or fluid.
夜 (yè) is close in sound to 液 — an exact match.
亻 (person) — 体 relates to the human body.
本 (běn) is close in sound to tǐ, and was chosen as a simplified phonetic substitute when 體 was simplified to 体.

example.hanzi: 水在常温下是液体,加热后会变成气体。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ zài chángwēn xià shì yètǐ, jiārè hòu huì biànchéng qìtǐ.
example.english: Water is a liquid at room temperature and turns into a gas when heated.
example.fact: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at standard room temperature, remaining fluid down to about -39°C. That property is why it was historically used in thermometers and barometers, before health concerns led to its phase-out.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
竹 (bamboo) — early written answers were inscribed on bamboo strips.
合 (hé) is close in sound to dá, and also carries the sense of 'to fit, correspond,' matching an answer to a question.

example.hanzi: 他决心努力工作来报答父母的养育之恩。
example.pinyin: Tā juéxīn nǔlì gōngzuò lái bàodá fùmǔ de yǎngyù zhī ēn.
example.english: He resolved to work hard to repay his parents for raising him.
example.fact: Vampire bats are one of the few mammals known to reciprocate favors: a bat that shares regurgitated blood with a hungry roost-mate is more likely to receive blood in return later. This was documented as a real-world example of reciprocal altruism by biologist Gerald Wilkinson in the 1980s.

components.note: 阝 (a mound, a place) — 阴 relates to the shaded side of a hill.
月 (moon) — the moon, associated with night and shade, gave 阴 its meaning 'shady, overcast'; compare 阳, which uses 日 (sun) for the opposite, sunny meaning.
艹 (grass/plant) — 茎 names the stem or stalk of a plant.

example.hanzi: 医生解释了阴茎的基本解剖结构。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiěshì le yīnjīng de jīběn jiěpōu jiégòu.
example.english: The doctor explained the basic anatomy of the penis.
example.fact: Relative to body size, the acorn barnacle has one of the longest penises in the animal kingdom, capable of extending several times its own body length to reach mates in neighboring shells. This is necessary because barnacles are immobile once they settle onto a surface.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) is a faint match in sound to 教's reading jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.
巳 (a place) — the destination being pointed toward, giving 导 its meaning 'to lead, guide, direct.'

example.hanzi: 老师的教导让我终身受益。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī de jiàodǎo ràng wǒ zhōngshēn shòuyì.
example.english: My teacher's instruction benefited me for my whole life.
example.fact: Aristotle tutored a young Alexander the Great for several years at the Macedonian court, instructing him in logic, medicine, and rhetoric. Alexander went on to build an empire stretching from Greece to India.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) is a faint match in sound to 特's reading tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
木 (wood) — 权 originally meant a wooden lever or weight, later extended to 'power, authority, right.'
雚 was historically closer to guàn; the pronunciation has since shifted to quán, so the sound link is faint today.

example.hanzi: 王室成员享有许多普通人没有的特权。
example.pinyin: Wángshì chéngyuán xiǎngyǒu xǔduō pǔtōngrén méiyǒu de tèquán.
example.english: Members of the royal family enjoy many privileges that ordinary people do not have.
example.fact: Diplomatic immunity, formalized in the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, grants foreign diplomats privileges such as exemption from local prosecution and taxation. The practice has roots going back to ancient protections for royal envoys.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恐 describes fear felt in the heart.
巩 (gǒng) is close in sound to kǒng, sharing the same rhyme.
A drawing of a long, coiling creature with a horned head, representing the mythical Chinese dragon.

example.hanzi: 博物馆里展出了一只巨大的恐龙化石。
example.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchū le yì zhī jùdà de kǒnglóng huàshí.
example.english: The museum displayed a huge dinosaur fossil.
example.fact: The largest dinosaur fossils belong to titanosaurs like Argentinosaurus, estimated to have weighed up to 90 tons and stretched over 30 meters long. That is roughly the length of three school buses end to end.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) is a sound hint for 英, pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
力 (strength) — 勇 describes inner strength shown as courage.
甬 (yǒng) is an exact match for the sound of 勇.

example.hanzi: 消防员英勇地冲进火场救人。
example.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán yīngyǒng de chōngjìn huǒchǎng jiùrén.
example.english: The firefighters heroically rushed into the fire to save people.
example.fact: During the 1966 Aberfan disaster in Wales, rescuers, including off-duty miners, dug through a collapsed coal-waste tip by hand for days trying to reach trapped villagers. The tragedy led to major changes in UK mine safety regulation.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 棍 names an object made of wood, a stick.
昆 (kūn) is close in sound to gùn, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他用一根棍子把苹果从树上打下来。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng yī gēn gùnzi bǎ píngguǒ cóng shù shàng dǎ xiàlái.
example.english: He used a stick to knock apples down from the tree.
example.fact: Chimpanzees in Gombe National Park, first documented by Jane Goodall in 1960, strip leaves from twigs to fashion simple tools used to fish termites out of their mounds. It is one of the earliest confirmed examples of tool use by a non-human animal.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — 魔 names a demon or evil spirit.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.
术 is a simplified form of 術, which combined 行 (a crossroads, a road) with a phonetic element — the idea of a path leading somewhere gave rise to 术's meaning 'skill, art, method.'
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'

example.hanzi: 那位魔术师的表演让观众目瞪口呆。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi móshùshī de biǎoyǎn ràng guānzhòng mùdèngkǒudāi.
example.english: That magician's performance left the audience astonished.
example.fact: Harry Houdini, born Erik Weisz in Budapest in 1874, built his reputation on escape acts, such as freeing himself from locked, water-filled milk cans. He spent his later career debunking fraudulent spiritualists who claimed to contact the dead.

meanings: (of number, time, size etc) just right

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 恰 describes something that fits exactly as intended.
合 (hé) gives a sound distantly related to qià, having drifted apart over time.
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 我到车站的时候,恰好赶上了末班车。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dào chēzhàn de shíhòu, qiàhǎo gǎn shàng le mòbānchē.
example.english: When I arrived at the station, I happened to catch the last bus just in time.
example.fact: Leap seconds are occasionally added to Coordinated Universal Time to keep clocks in sync with Earth's slightly irregular rotation. This ensures that global timekeeping stays just right relative to the actual length of a day.

components.note: 米 depicts scattered grains of husked rice around a central stalk — a simple picture giving 米 its meaning 'rice, grain.'
Yawn — associated with tiredness and needing rest.
Gives the sound hé, related to xiē but drifted apart over time.

尔 is a simplified form of 爾, an ancient character whose original picture — possibly a decorative net or woven pattern — is now obscure. It was borrowed early on for its sound to write the pronoun 'you' and, in transliterations, a neutral final syllable.

example.hanzi: 米歇尔是这次会议的主讲人。
example.pinyin: Mǐxiē'ěr shì zhè cì huìyì de zhǔjiǎngrén.
example.english: Michel is the keynote speaker at this conference.
example.fact: U.S. Senator George Mitchell chaired the multi-party talks that produced the 1998 Good Friday Agreement. The agreement largely ended three decades of sectarian violence known as the Troubles in Northern Ireland.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — taste is sensed on the tongue.
甘 (sweet, tasty) contributes to the character's form, naming the flavor itself.
羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'

example.hanzi: 她笑起来的样子很甜美。
example.pinyin: Tā xiào qǐlái de yàngzi hěn tiánměi.
example.english: Her smile looks very sweet.
example.fact: Honey is one of the few foods that essentially never spoils, because its low moisture content and high acidity create an environment hostile to bacteria. Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs more than 3,000 years old that was reportedly still edible.

components.note: 犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 在这个国家,乱扔垃圾也算犯法。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège guójiā, luàn rēng lājī yě suàn fànfǎ.
example.english: In this country, littering is also considered breaking the law.
example.fact: Singapore enforces some of the world's strictest anti-littering laws, with fines that can exceed 2,000 Singapore dollars for repeat offenders. Repeat offenders can also be handed mandatory Corrective Work Orders that require them to clean public spaces in reflective vests.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 势 relates to power, force, and influence
执 (zhí) has a loose sound connection to 势's reading shì
力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.hanzi: 这个家族在当地拥有很大的势力。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiāzú zài dāngdì yǒngyǒu hěn dà de shìli.
example.english: This family holds great power and influence in the local area.
example.fact: The Medici family, through control of banking in 15th-century Florence, wielded such immense political influence that four Medici men became popes. The family effectively ruled the Florentine Republic for generations without holding an official hereditary title.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) is close in sound to 认, pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.
丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) is close in sound to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud

example.hanzi: 这项新技术还没有得到官方认可。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng xīn jìshù hái méiyǒu dédào guānfāng rènkě.
example.english: This new technology has not yet received official approval.
example.fact: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's approval process for a new drug typically takes over a decade and can cost more than a billion dollars. It covers multiple phases of clinical trials before the agency grants official approval for public use.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'
户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'

example.hanzi: 请在表格上填写您的永久住所地址。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài biǎogé shàng tiánxiě nín de yǒngjiǔ zhùsuǒ dìzhǐ.
example.english: Please fill in your permanent residence address on the form.
example.fact: Çatalhöyük, a Neolithic settlement in modern-day Turkey dating to around 7500 BC, housed thousands of people in densely packed mudbrick residences with no streets between them. Residents entered their homes through holes in the roof.

components.note: 求 originally pictured a fur coat, its ancient form showing tufts of fur along a garment. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the unrelated meaning 'to seek, request.'
力 (strength) — 助 relates to helping, lending one's strength
且 (qiě) has a loose sound connection to 助's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 遇到困难时,不要害怕向别人求助。
example.pinyin: Yùdào kùnnán shí, búyào hàipà xiàng biérén qiúzhù.
example.english: When facing difficulties, don't be afraid to seek help from others.
example.fact: The distress signal SOS, adopted internationally in 1906, was chosen not as an acronym but because its Morse code pattern of three dots, three dashes, three dots is simple and unmistakable to transmit and recognize under pressure.

components.note: 攵 (an action/to strike) — ties to 致's sense of bringing about or causing an effect
至 (zhì) is close in sound to 致 — an exact match
苟 (to be careful, cautious) — conveys the reverent carefulness at the heart of 敬's meaning 'to respect.'
攵 (an action, a hand with a stick) — adds the sense of an outward act, such as a bow or gesture, performed to show respect.

example.hanzi: 士兵们向国旗致敬。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen xiàng guóqí zhìjìng.
example.english: The soldiers saluted the national flag.
example.fact: The military hand salute is thought by some historians to descend from medieval knights raising their visors to show their face and peaceful intent, though the exact origin is debated among historians.

components.note: 广 (wide) — 扩 relates to making something wider or bigger.
扌 also carries a sound value in this simplified character, distantly related to kuò.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 公司计划扩大在海外的业务。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī jìhuà kuòdà zài hǎiwài de yèwù.
example.english: The company plans to expand its overseas business.
example.fact: In 1929, astronomer Edwin Hubble observed that distant galaxies are moving away from us at speeds proportional to their distance. This provided key evidence that the universe itself is continuously expanding.

components.note: 你 (you) — the base pronoun
心 (heart) — added below to show warmth and respect toward the listener
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 您好,请问有什么可以帮您的吗?
example.pinyin: Nínhǎo, qǐngwèn yǒu shénme kěyǐ bāng nín de ma?
example.english: Hello, how may I help you?
example.fact: In traditional Japanese business etiquette, the depth and duration of a bow used in greeting varies by rank and occasion. A 45-degree bow called saikeirei is reserved for the deepest apologies or greatest respect, while a much shallower bow suffices for everyday greetings.

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 厨师把披萨四分,分给四个孩子。
example.pinyin: Chúshī bǎ pīsà sìfēn, fēn gěi sì gè háizi.
example.english: The chef divided the pizza into four parts, giving one to each of four children.
example.fact: American football games are divided into four 15-minute quarters, a structural choice inherited from early 20th-century college football rules. The setup gave teams scheduled breaks for strategy and rest.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 每年春节,他都会回老家看望父母。
example.pinyin: Měinián Chūnjié, tā dōu huì huí lǎojiā kànwàng fùmǔ.
example.english: Every Spring Festival, he goes back to his hometown to visit his parents.
example.fact: Chunyun, the Chinese New Year travel rush, is considered the largest annual human migration on Earth, with an estimated three billion trips made across China in a single travel season. Most travelers are returning to their home regions to be with family.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'

example.hanzi: 在物理学中,爱因斯坦提出了相对论。
example.pinyin: Zài wùlǐxué zhōng, Àiyīnsītǎn tíchū le xiāngduìlùn.
example.english: In physics, Einstein proposed the theory of relativity.
example.fact: Einstein's theory of general relativity, published in 1915, predicts that massive objects bend spacetime. That prediction was confirmed in 1919 when astronomers observed starlight bending around the sun during a total solar eclipse.

components.note: 单 is a simplified form of 單, whose ancient shape pictured a forked hunting tool resembling a slingshot held in the hand. The character was later borrowed for the unrelated meaning 'single, one, simple.'
纟 (silk/thread) — 纯 originally described unmixed, undyed silk thread, extending to 'pure, unmixed.'
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to chún, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 孩子的想法往往很单纯。
example.pinyin: Háizi de xiǎngfǎ wǎngwǎng hěn dānchún.
example.english: Children's thoughts are often very simple and pure.
example.fact: Diamond and graphite are both made of pure carbon in its simplest elemental form. Yet the different arrangement of their atoms gives one unmatched hardness and the other enough softness to write with.

components.note: The outline pictures a bent, curved container or musical instrument, giving 曲 its meaning 'crooked, bent' and, by extension, 'a tune.'
木 (wood) — 棍 names an object made of wood, a stick.
昆 (kūn) is close in sound to gùn, sharing the same rhyme and a related initial.
王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) is close in sound to 球 — an exact match

example.hanzi: 曲棍球是一项需要团队合作的运动。
example.pinyin: Qūgùnqiú shì yī xiàng xūyào tuánduì hézuò de yùndòng.
example.english: Field hockey is a sport that requires teamwork.
example.fact: Field hockey is believed to have origins stretching back over 4,000 years, with stick-and-ball games depicted in ancient Egyptian tomb art at Beni Hasan. That makes it one of the oldest team sports still played today.

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
二 (two) — 些 originally suggested a small plural amount, building on the idea of 'more than one.'
此 (cǐ) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches the modern reading xiē.

example.hanzi: 书架上好些书都还没有看完。
example.pinyin: Shūjià shàng hǎoxiē shū dōu hái méiyǒu kàn wán.
example.english: There are quite a lot of books on the shelf that haven't been finished yet.
example.fact: The Library of Congress in Washington, D.C. holds more than 170 million items across its collections, including books, manuscripts, maps, and recordings. That makes it the largest library in the world by shelf space.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) is close in sound to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
亻 (person) — 信 relates to what a person says.
言 (speech, words) — a person standing by their words gave 信 its meaning 'trust, honesty' and, later, 'a letter.'

example.hanzi: 记者必须核实消息来源是否可信。
example.pinyin: Jìzhě bìxū héshí xiāoxī láiyuán shìfǒu kěxìn.
example.english: Journalists must verify whether their sources are trustworthy.
example.fact: Fact-checking as an organized newsroom practice dates back to the 1920s at magazines like Time, where dedicated checkers verified every factual claim in an article before publication. The practice was created specifically to protect the outlet's credibility.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) is a faint match in sound to 资's reading zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
厂 (chǎng) is a sound hint for 产's reading chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.

example.hanzi: 这家公司的总资产超过十亿美元。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de zǒng zīchǎn chāoguò shí yì měiyuán.
example.english: This company's total assets exceed one billion US dollars.
example.fact: Studies by valuation firm Ocean Tomo have found that intangible assets, such as patents, brand value, and data, now make up the large majority of the total market value of S&P 500 companies. That share has grown steadily since the mid-20th century, when physical assets dominated corporate balance sheets.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 锤 names a metal tool.
垂 (chuí) is close in sound to 锤's reading — an exact match.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他用锤子把钉子敲进木板里。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng chuízi bǎ dìngzi qiāo jìn mùbǎn lǐ.
example.english: He used a hammer to knock the nail into the board.
example.fact: Stone hammerstones found at the Lomekwi site in Kenya date back roughly 3.3 million years, predating the genus Homo. That suggests an even earlier hominin species crafted them, making hammers among the oldest tools known.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
亻 (person) — 什 originally referred to a group of people.
十 (ten) — combined with 亻 (person), 什 originally described a group of ten; the character later came to be used for the common word 什么 (what).

example.hanzi: 乔治·布什曾任美国第41任总统。
example.pinyin: Qiáozhì Bùshí céng rèn Měiguó dì sìshíyī rèn zǒngtǒng.
example.english: George Bush once served as the 41st President of the United States.
example.fact: George H. W. Bush, the 41st U.S. president, previously served as director of the CIA and as a naval aviator during World War II. He survived after being shot down over the Pacific in 1944.

components.note: 录 traditionally depicted a hand-held tool used for carving or writing records — the image behind its meaning 'to record, to write down.'
又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'

example.hanzi: 她被那所大学录取了,全家都很高兴。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi nà suǒ dàxué lùqǔ le, quánjiā dōu hěn gāoxìng.
example.english: She was admitted to that university, and the whole family was delighted.
example.fact: Harvard University's undergraduate admission rate has fallen below 4% in recent years. That makes it one of the most selective universities in the world despite receiving tens of thousands of applications annually.

components.note: 东 (simplified from 東) originally pictured the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木 — since the sun rises in the east, the character came to mean 'east.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 美国东部沿海地区人口非常密集。
example.pinyin: Měiguó dōngbù yánhǎi dìqū rénkǒu fēicháng mìjí.
example.english: The eastern coastal region of the United States is very densely populated.
example.fact: The eastern seaboard of the United States, stretching from Maine to Florida, is home to roughly a third of the country's population. That share of people lives on a relatively small fraction of the nation's total land area.

meanings: (fig.) to make an identical copy of (a website etc)

components.note: 十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
阝 (a mound or hill) — 隆 relates to something rising high or being abundant, like a swelling mound.
夅, related to 降, is close in sound to lóng and contributes to the character's pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 1996年,科学家成功克隆出了一只名叫多莉的羊。
example.pinyin: 1996 nián, kēxuéjiā chénggōng kèlóng chū le yī zhī míng jiào Duōlì de yáng.
example.english: In 1996, scientists successfully cloned a sheep named Dolly.
example.fact: Dolly the sheep, born in 1996 at the Roslin Institute in Scotland, was the first mammal successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell. The breakthrough reshaped scientific and ethical debates about cloning technology.

components.note: 囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 他大学毕业后就去国外工作了。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu jiù qù guówài gōngzuò le.
example.english: After graduating from university, he went abroad to work.
example.fact: According to UNESCO estimates, more than six million students were enrolled in higher education outside their home country in recent years. The United States, United Kingdom, and Australia rank among the most common destinations.

components.note: Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 警察要求他交出驾驶证。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá yāoqiú tā jiāochū jiàshǐzhèng.
example.english: The police asked him to hand over his driver's license.
example.fact: At the end of World War II, Japan formally surrendered aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay on September 2, 1945. Representatives handed over signed documents of unconditional surrender to Allied commanders.

components.note: A pictograph of an ancient forked weapon, such as a club or shield-tipped spear — the tool image later extended to 干's meanings 'to do, to work' and, in another reading, 'dry.'
酉 (originally 'wine jar,' broadened to fermented foods) — 酪 names fermented dairy products like cheese and koumiss.
各 (gè) is the phonetic element from the character's history, but its modern reading no longer resembles 酪's lào — the connection today is historical rather than audible.

example.hanzi: 这种干酪需要在地窖中陈放至少六个月。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng gānlào xūyào zài dìjiào zhōng chénfàng zhìshǎo liù gè yuè.
example.english: This cheese needs to age in a cellar for at least six months.
example.fact: Some wheels of Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese are aged for over three years and can weigh close to 40 kilograms. Italian producers have even used them as loan collateral at specialized cheese banks that store and insure the aging wheels.

components.note: 敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) is a sound hint for 整, pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'

example.hanzi: 越来越多的人选择整形手术来改善外貌。
example.pinyin: Yuè lái yuè duō de rén xuǎnzé zhěngxíng shǒushù lái gǎishàn wàimào.
example.english: More and more people are choosing plastic surgery to improve their appearance.
example.fact: Reconstructive surgery techniques for the nose date back over 2,600 years to the ancient Indian physician Sushruta. His text, the Sushruta Samhita, described skin-flap grafting methods still recognizable in modern rhinoplasty.

components.note: 氵 (water) — sand forms as water erodes rock over time.
少 (shǎo) shares the initial sh- with shā, though the vowel has since shifted.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上用沙子堆城堡。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng yòng shāzi duī chéngbǎo.
example.english: The children built castles out of sand on the beach.
example.fact: Construction-grade sand is in global short supply despite deserts being full of it, because desert sand grains are too round and smooth from wind erosion to bind well in concrete. Builders instead rely on angular sand mined from riverbeds and quarries.

components.note: ⺊ (a divination crack/omen) — a sign to be interpreted
口 (mouth) — speaking the meaning of the omen aloud
页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) is a sound hint for 领, pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 军队迅速占领了这座城市。
example.pinyin: Jūnduì xùnsù zhànlǐng le zhè zuò chéngshì.
example.english: The army quickly occupied the city.
example.fact: Following World War II, Allied forces occupied Japan from 1945 to 1952 under General Douglas MacArthur. During that period, a new constitution renouncing war was drafted and adopted.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) is close in sound to 注's reading zhù
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) is close in sound to 视 — an exact match.

example.hanzi: 全世界的目光都注视着这场比赛。
example.pinyin: Quán shìjiè de mùguāng dōu zhùshì zhe zhè chǎng bǐsài.
example.english: The eyes of the whole world are watching this match closely.
example.fact: The peregrine falcon, whose eyesight is estimated to be up to eight times sharper than a human's, can spot prey on the ground from over a kilometer high. It then dives at speeds exceeding 300 kilometers per hour to make the catch.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
宓 depicts stillness and quiet beneath a roof.
山 (mountain) — a quiet, secluded mountain gave 密 its meaning 'dense, secret, close.'

example.hanzi: 所有的用户密码都经过加密存储。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǒu de yònghù mìmǎ dōu jīngguò jiāmì cúnchú.
example.english: All user passwords are stored after being encrypted.
example.fact: During World War II, the German military's Enigma machine encrypted messages using rotating wheels that created billions of possible settings. Codebreakers at Bletchley Park, including Alan Turing, developed methods to crack it.

components.note: 大 (big, a person with arms and legs spread) pictures a person.
镸 (long) pictures a long piece of cloth wrapped around them, giving 套 its meaning 'cover, case.'
户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) is close in sound to 房, pronounced fáng, a close match

example.hanzi: 这家酒店的套房带有独立的客厅。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de tàofáng dài yǒu dúlì de kètīng.
example.english: This hotel's suite comes with a separate living room.
example.fact: The Royal Suite at Raffles Hotel in Singapore, opened in 1887, has hosted guests including Rudyard Kipling and Elizabeth Taylor. The hotel is also credited as the birthplace of the Singapore Sling cocktail in 1915.

components.note: 风 (wind) — 飓 names a violent storm, a hurricane.
具 (jù) is close in sound to 飓 — an exact match.
凡 (fán) is a distant phonetic root for 风's reading fēng, drifted apart over time.
虫 (insect) — an ancient belief held that wind could give rise to small creatures, linking 风 to this symbol.

example.hanzi: 飓风即将登陆,居民被要求撤离。
example.pinyin: Jùfēng jíjiāng dēnglù, jūmín bèi yāoqiú chèlí.
example.english: The hurricane is about to make landfall, and residents have been ordered to evacuate.
example.fact: Hurricane Patricia in 2015 reached sustained winds of about 345 km/h (215 mph) in the eastern Pacific, making it one of the most intense tropical cyclones ever recorded at sea. It weakened significantly before making landfall.
